title: (No AI) Guitar company D’Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![D’Addario logo imposed over image of a person playing guitar.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/1583922033086.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Maybe don’t let the AI shred next time. | Image: D’Addario

After weeks of controversy and speculation, music company D'Addario has [admitted](https://guitar.com/news/industry-news/daddario-admit-ai-controversy/) that AI, specifically Suno, was used as part of a recent promotional video. For nearly two weeks, the company has [denied the allegations](https://www.guitarworld.com/gear/guitar-strings/daddario-denies-using-ai-in-string-demo-video), even as evidence piled up against it. It offered various explanations, from low-quality exports, to combinations of plugins like Autotune introducing digital noise, and the use of AI-assisted mastering tools from LANDR and Logic. But now the company has edited its original Instagram post denying the use of generative AI to say it was wrong.

In a lengthy update to [its post from July 29th](https://www.instagram.com/daddarioandco/p/DbYvntjIOzg/) (embedded at the bottom), it said:

> W …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/978982/daddario-guitar-ai-music-suno)

title: (No AI) Google’s Pixel Watch 5 dives deeper into AI and health
author: Victoria Song
content:
![Pixel watch 5 on its dock with a colorful rainbow textile strap. The pixel buds 2 are in the background.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Google-Pixel-Watch-5-on-stand.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

At least there’s no new proprietary charger this year. Huzzah!! | Photo: David Imel / The Verge

The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 isn't about the hardware. Sure, there's a new satin pyrite case finish, a few new strap colors, and a Steph Curry Special Edition. Under the hood, there's a slightly faster Qualcomm processor and an itty-bitty battery bump. There's a $50 price hike from last year, too, because the Pixel Watch 5 isn't immune to RAMageddon - none of us are. Otherwise, no one would blame you for looking at this watch and thinking absolutely nothing's changed. That's because the big updates this year are all software-based.

This isn't a huge surprise considering [Google's Fitbit Air](https://www.theverge.com/tech/954768/google-fitbit-air-review-fitness-tracker-wearable-ai-health-coach) launch in May. And after seeing some Pixel Watch 5 …
